verses.author: model_A
verses.text: A boat leaves the harbor before anyone is awake to see it go.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left the porch light on anyway,
a small stubbornness against the dark,
believing brightness travels back to those who need it.
motifs: light traveling to those in need

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The boat won't see it either,
already past the point of turning back,
but the light keeps burning anyway,
a promise made to no one in particular.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone has to keep faith without an audience,
so the moths gather instead,
believers in whatever burns.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Their small bodies against the glass all night,
a kind of prayer with no words in it,
just wings saying *still here, still here.*

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
By morning some of them lie still on the sill,
proof that faith has a body,
that it can be swept away like anything else.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone will lift the broom in an hour,
not unkind, just moving on,
and the sill will be bare again,
ready for whatever else believes.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I sweep my own floor the same way,
tender to the dust,
never asking what it wanted.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The dustpan fills with names I never learned,
small grey weather of a life,
and still I carry it outside gently,
as if it might complain.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The wind takes it without thanks,
scatters what I meant to bury with care —
some things are only ever half-released.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
I open my palm to check —
a little grey still clings there,
not enough to name, enough to keep.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I wash my hands anyway,
knowing water won't reach
what the skin has already agreed to keep.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The towel darkens where I press it,
small grey ghost of an agreement,
and I hang it back up
like nothing was decided.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Later someone else will dry their hands there,
never knowing what they're taking on,
and hang it back the same careless way.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
By morning the towel's just a towel again —
though something in the weave remembers,
folding grey into white, quiet as breath.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I unfold it anyway, expecting nothing,
and something in me settles
the way water settles into a low place
without asking to be asked.
